{{ElectionsMO}}

The '''governor of Missouri''' is the [[head of government]] of the [[U.S. state]] of [[Missouri]] and the [[commander-in-chief]] of the  [[Missouri National Guard]]. The [[Governor (United States)|governor]] has a duty to enforce state laws and the power to either approve or [[veto]] bills passed by the [[Missouri General Assembly|Missouri Legislature]], to convene the legislature and grant [[pardon]]s, except in cases of impeachment.

The current governor is [[Missouri Republican Party|Republican]] [[Mike Kehoe]], who took office on January 13, 2025.  

==List of governors==
[[Louisiana (New France)|Louisiana]] was [[Louisiana Purchase|purchased]] from France in 1803, with it being proclaimed in [[St. Louis]] in [[Illinois Country|Upper Louisiana]] on [[Three Flags Day|March 10, 1804]], by [[Amos Stoddard]], who remained as military commander of the region until October 1, 1804, when [[Orleans Territory]] was split from it. The remainder was designated the [[District of Louisiana]] and placed under the jurisdiction of [[Indiana Territory]] and its governor, [[William Henry Harrison]].<ref>{{usstat|2|283}}</ref>

===Louisiana Territory and Missouri Territory===
The [[District of Louisiana]] was organized as [[Louisiana Territory]] on July 4, 1805;<ref>{{usstat|2|331}}</ref> it was renamed [[Missouri Territory]] on June 4, 1812, after the admission of the state of [[Louisiana]].<ref>{{usstat|2|743}}</ref> It had four governors appointed by the [[president of the United States]], including both [[Meriwether Lewis]] and [[William Clark]] of the [[Lewis and Clark Expedition]].

===State of Missouri===
[[Missouri]] was [[admission to the Union|admitted to the union]] on August 10, 1821.<ref>{{usstat|3|545}}</ref> 

The original constitution of 1820 created the offices of governor and lieutenant governor, to serve terms of four years{{sfn|Thorpe|1909|p=2156|loc=1820 art. IV, § 3}} without being able to succeed themselves.{{sfn|Thorpe|1909|p=2156|loc=1820 art. IV, § 4}} Terms were shortened to 2 years in 1865,{{sfn|Thorpe|1909|p=2204|loc=1865 art. V, § 3}} with a limit of serving no more than four out of every six years.{{sfn|Thorpe|1909|p=2204|loc=1865 art. V, § 4}} They were returned in 1875 to the four-year term and limit on succession of the 1820 constitution,{{sfn|Thorpe|1909|p=2244|loc=1875 art. V, § 2}} and the term limit changed to two terms in 1965.<ref name="amendments">{{cite web |url=http://ipp.missouri.edu/files/ipp/attachments/19-2010_constitutional_amendments.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120522110915/http://ipp.missouri.edu/files/ipp/attachments/19-2010_constitutional_amendments.pdf |archive-date=May 22, 2012 |title=Constitutional Amendments, Statutory Revision and Referenda Submitted to the Voters by the General Assembly or by Initiative Petition, 1910–2010 |last=Valentine |first=David C. |date=December 2010 |publisher=University of Missouri Institute for Public Policy |access-date=March 24, 2023}}</ref> Originally, the lieutenant governor would act as governor in the event of a vacancy;{{sfn|Thorpe|1909|p=2157|loc=1820 art. IV, § 16}} a 1968 amendment made it so that the lieutenant governor becomes governor in that situation.<ref name="amendments" />

A group including the governor, lieutenant governor, and members of the [[Missouri General Assembly]], proclaimed Missouri's secession from the [[Union (American Civil War)|Union]] on October 31, 1861,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Secession Ordinances of 13 Confederate States |url=http://www.digitalhistory.uh.edu/disp_textbook.cfm?smtID=3&psid=3953 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905091739/http://www.digitalhistory.uh.edu/disp_textbook.cfm?smtID=3&psid=3953 |archive-date=September 5, 2015 |access-date=May 24, 2015 |publisher=[[University of Houston]]}}</ref> and it was admitted to the [[Confederate States of America]] on November 28, 1861.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=dul1.ark:/13960/t2t44fh2r&seq=243 |page=221 |title=The Statutes at Large of the Provisional Government of the Confederate States of America |editor-last=Matthews |editor-first=James M. |year=1864 |location=Richmond, Virginia |publisher=R.M. Smith |via=[[HathiTrust]]}}</ref> The Confederate government elected two governors, but only had any control in the south of the state, and was forced into exile in [[Marshall, Texas]], after the [[Battle of Pea Ridge]] in March 1862.

==Timeline==
{| role="presentation" class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed"
| <strong>Timeline of Missouri governors</strong>
|-
|
<div class="center">{{#tag:timeline
|ImageSize = width:1500 height:auto barincrement:18
PlotArea   = top:10 bottom:20 right:130 left:10
AlignBars  = late
DateFormat = x.y
Period     = from:1804.90 till:{{#expr:{{#time:Y}}+{{#time:m}}/6}}
TimeAxis   = orientation:horizontal
ScaleMajor = unit:year increment:10 start:1810
ScaleMinor = unit:year increment:1 start:1805

Define $now = {{#expr:{{#time:Y}}+{{#time:m}}/12}}

Colors =
  id:5year    value:rgb(0.8, 0.8, 0.8)
  id:0year    value:rgb(0.6, 0.6, 0.6)
  id:noparty  value:rgb(0.7, 0.7, 0.7)
  id:demrep   value:rgb(0, 0.5, 0)
  id:dem      value:rgb(0.2, 0.2, 1)
  id:unionist value:rgb(1, 0.67, 0.8)
  id:rep      value:rgb(0.91, 0.11, 0.14)
  id:librep   value:rgb(1, 0.41, 0.71)
  id:seat1    value:rgb(0.60, 0.10, 0.10)
  id:blank    value:white

BarData =
  barset:GovernorLine
  barset:Governors
  #barset:blankline

==Confederate governors==

[[File:Thomas-c-reynolds.jpg|upright|thumb|[[Thomas Caute Reynolds]], 2nd Confederate governor of Missouri]]
[[Missouri in the American Civil War|During the Civil War]], after the capture of [[Jefferson City, Missouri|Jefferson City]] by the Union, a [[Missouri Constitutional Convention of 1861–1863|constitutional convention]] declared the office then held by Governor [[Claiborne Fox Jackson]] to be vacant.<ref name="convention" /> In October, Jackson, Lieutenant Governor [[Thomas Caute Reynolds]], and some members of the General Assembly, organized at [[Neosho, Missouri|Neosho]] and [[Missouri secession|passed]] an [[Ordinance of Secession]]. This [[Confederate government of Missouri|Confederate government]] never displaced the government in [[Jefferson City, Missouri|Jefferson City]], and Missouri remained in the Union through the entire war. Jackson continued on as governor until his death on December 6, 1862, at which time Reynolds took over, serving until he fled to Mexico in June 1865 after the end of the war.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Geise |first=William R. |date=1962 |title=Missouri's Confederate Capital in Marshall, Texas |journal=The Southwestern Historical Quarterly |volume=66 |issue=2 |page=206 |issn=0038-478X |jstor=30236239}}</ref>
